key_insight: A first-principles phonon-transport model best captures heat conduction in AlGaN HEMT thin-film layers, yielding the most physically consistent results among three models compared.
engineering_relevance: Reliable thermal-conductivity modeling can support buffer and transition layer design for improved heat management in HEMT devices.
method: Compare three phonon-transport models, from a Debye approximation to DFT-derived harmonic and anharmonic phonon properties.
Establish intrinsic transport dominated by Umklapp scattering, then add alloy, grain-boundary, and film-boundary scattering.
Fit boundary-scattering contributions to time-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR) thermal-conductivity measurements.
evidence_signal: Comparison with TDTR measurements supports the first-principles model as the best-performing approach, though the abstract reports no quantitative error metrics.
watch_item: Boundary-scattering parameters are fitted to specific samples, so transferability to other thin-film microstructures requires validation.
paper_title: Thermal investigation of buffer and transition layers in AlGaN HEMT stacks
